Estimating VRAM available for local AI on both devices.

The Linux desktop uses an AMD iGPU that shares system RAM rather than dedicated VRAM. The MacBook Pro M4 has 24GB of unified memory. Both devices lack discrete graphics cards.

The Radeon 740M is an RDNA 3 iGPU on Phoenix2. Its shared VRAM is typically carved out in BIOS, often 512MB to 4GB. Local AI inference on this card depends on driver support and the configured carve-out size.

AMD iGPU AI support on Linux is spottier than on NVIDIA or Apple Silicon. The 8500G's 740M draws all compute memory from the 32GB system pool. Realistic usable VRAM for local AI inference is likely only a few gigabytes. ROCm and OpenCL support for RDNA 3 iGPUs remains limited.

The MacBook Pro M4 can allocate roughly 16–18 GB of its 24 GB unified memory for ML workloads. The GPU accesses the same memory pool as the CPU. Models run efficiently with Metal backends like MLX and llama.cpp.

The 8500G’s 740M can only deliver 8–16 GB of shared VRAM for AI workloads. ROCm does not officially support RDNA 3 iGPUs for machine learning. The unified memory on the MacBook Pro M4 is dynamically allocated rather than fixed.

The M4 Neural Engine runs ML tasks independently and does not consume unified memory. Model weights can occupy roughly 18–22 GB on the MacBook Pro while macOS reserves 2–6 GB for itself. The 8500G’s 740M carries only 4–8 RDNA3 compute units. Its memory bandwidth is shared with the CPU over DDR5.

On the MacBook Pro M4, a 13B parameter model at Q4 should run comfortably within the 24 GB unified memory pool. A 32B quantized model is possible only with aggressive memory management. The Linux desktop shows roughly 30.5 GB of usable system RAM, though the integrated Radeon 740M has no dedicated VRAM.

_**Agent (auto-low)**_

Short answer: neither machine has separate VRAM like an NVIDIA GPU. Both use **shared system RAM**. The Mac is much better for local AI because Apple Silicon actually lets the GPU use most of that pool efficiently.

## Linux desktop (Ryzen 5 8500G + Radeon 740M, 32 GB RAM)

Your system reports:

| Pool | Size | What it means |
|------|------|----------------|
| **Visible VRAM** (BIOS carve-out) | **512 MB** | Fixed framebuffer reservation |
| **GTT** (GPU-accessible shared RAM) | **~15.2 GB** | What Vulkan/llama.cpp can use on Linux |
| **System RAM** (CPU inference) | **~30 GB** total | Full pool if you run CPU-only |

**For local AI on this box:**

- **GPU path (Vulkan llama.cpp, etc.):** roughly **12–15 GB** usable for model weights, depending on how much RAM you leave for Cinnamon, browser, Cursor, etc.
- **CPU path (Ollama/llama.cpp CPU):** up to **~25–28 GB** for models, since you're not fighting a VRAM cap — but tokens/sec will be slower.
- **ROCm:** not really an option here; the 740M isn't well supported for ML on Linux.

**Reality check:** memory isn't the main limit — the **740M is tiny** (4 RDNA3 CUs). Even a 7B Q4 model (~4.5 GB) may barely fit in the GPU pool. Bigger models should run **CPU-only** on your 32 GB RAM. You also have **no swap**, so loading something too large will OOM instead of gracefully swapping.

---

## MacBook Pro M4, 24 GB RAM

| Pool | Size | What it means |
|------|------|----------------|
| **Unified memory** | **24 GB** total | CPU, GPU, and Neural Engine share one pool |
| **Default GPU-usable** | **~16–18 GB** | macOS + Metal typically reserve ~6–8 GB for the OS |
| **Tuned ceiling** | **~20–22 GB** | With `iogpu.wired_limit_mb` sysctl (use carefully) |

**For local AI on the Mac:**

- **Comfortable:** 7B–14B at Q4/Q8 (MLX or Ollama)
- **Tight but possible:** 27B–32B at Q4 if you close other apps
- **Not realistic:** 70B+ on 24 GB

The M4's advantage isn't just capacity — **Metal/MLX is mature**, and unified memory has no PCIe copy overhead. Even base M4 (120 GB/s bandwidth) will feel much faster than your 740M for inference. If it's an **M4 Pro** with 24 GB, you get **273 GB/s** bandwidth, which helps tokens/sec further.

---

## Side-by-side

| | Linux 8500G desktop | MacBook Pro M4 24GB |
|---|---|---|
| **Dedicated VRAM** | None (512 MB BIOS carve-out only) | None |
| **Best GPU-usable pool** | ~12–15 GB (GTT) | ~16–18 GB (default) |
| **Max practical for AI** | ~25–28 GB (CPU-only) | ~20–22 GB (tuned, all-in) |
| **Sweet spot models** | 7B CPU, maybe 7B GPU | 7B–14B GPU, 32B if careful |
| **Framework** | llama.cpp Vulkan or CPU | MLX, Ollama (MLX backend), Metal |

**Bottom line:** treat the Mac as having **~18 GB of effective "VRAM"** for local LLMs out of the box. Treat the Linux box as **~15 GB on GPU** or **~28 GB on CPU** — but for actual AI work, the Mac wins on both software support and speed. Your desktop's 32 GB RAM is better for running larger models slowly on CPU than for GPU acceleration.

If you want, I can suggest specific model sizes/quantizations for each machine based on what you're trying to run (coding assistant, chat, image gen, etc.).

---

The **WebFX-G15** sets the floor: anything that works on all three must fit **~5 GB VRAM**. The useful **two-of-three** pair is **Linux + Mac** — the Windows laptop blocks Tier 1 and Tier 2 dense models.

## Top 5 — all three machines

| # | Model | Why |
|---|-------|-----|
| 1 | **Gemma 3 4B** | ~2.2 GB at Q4. Comfortable on the 6 GB card; still useful on Linux and Mac. |
| 2 | **Qwen3 8B** | Best dense quality that clears all three. ~5 GB at Q4 — tight on the G15; keep context short. |
| 3 | **Llama 3.2 3B** | Fastest on every GPU. Good sanity-check model. |
| 4 | **Qwen2.5-Coder 7B** | ~4.7 GB. Cross-platform coding default for PHP/theme work. |
| 5 | **Bonsai 27B** (1-bit) | ~4 GB. 27B-class reasoning in a Tier 0 footprint. Different install per OS (CUDA / Vulkan / MLX), but fits every GPU. |

**Fails the all-three test:** Qwen3 14B, Gemma 3 12B, and dense 27B/32B builds — fine on Linux and Mac, too heavy for 6 GB VRAM + 16 GB RAM on Windows.

---

## Top 5 — two of three (Linux + Mac)

The pair that matters. Both have room above the G15.

| # | Model | Skips |
|---|-------|-------|
| 1 | **Qwen3 14B** | Windows (~8–10 GB at Q4) |
| 2 | **Gemma 3 12B** | Windows (~7.5 GB at Q4) |
| 3 | **Qwen2.5-Coder 14B** | Windows |
| 4 | **Qwen3 27B** | Windows (16 GB RAM wall; Linux CPU overnight + Mac Tier 2) |
| 5 | **Qwen2.5 32B** | Windows (same) |

**Mac + Windows** and **Linux + Windows** don't get separate lists — anything that fits both laptops is already in the all-three table, or it's Bonsai again.

---

**Practical rule:** sync one **all-three** model everywhere (**Gemma 3 4B** or **Qwen3 8B**), then keep **Qwen3 14B** on Linux and Mac when you need more brain.

Added this as **"Models that work across machines"** in `__local-ai-my-machines.md`.
